main_text.p: feriem, deniq; institutum & verba expendere malo. ista enim quam affingis enarrationem satis su-perq; revincent.

Non nescis arbitror, in eo libro Tertullianum conari asserere carnis resurrectionem (ut titulus ipse indicat) adversus multos qui tum eam impetebant. Id ut faciat, multa conatur: illud autem in primis, ut Dei in carnem beneficia siue (ut ipse uocat) praerogatiuas enumeret, atq; amplificet. Inter alias multas, istas recenset, quòd salutis ea velut cardo sit: & quae dum est in carne anima non crediderit, seruari non possit: deniq; quae ad salutem faciunt animae, Deum ea per carnem ipsi suggerere atq; subministrare. Ac tum velut gradatione utitur a Baptismo ad Dominicam coenam, hoc est a primo ad postremum usq; gradum enume-rans quae sacramenta erant, & sacramentorū speciem tum habebant: ut velut per inductionē probaret, animam quae ad salutem suam efficiendam pertinent, per carnem accipere omnia. Ut clarius Tertulliani institutum peruideas, in tabulae for-mam locum totum oculis subiiciam.
Nunc Tilemanne confidera attentè, quid agat Tertullianus:

page.notes: The diagram is an outline as the brackets show. The levels are read from the brackets and are approximate. "ut ani-ma" sits between the two groups and is shown as one box. The label "Bapt." and the box "Signatum e-rant minimè mania" are read as one group on the right; the label "Cœna." stands on the row of "de Deo". Doubtful readings: "mania" at the end of the box "Signatum..." (perhaps "manu"); "faginctur" in "de Deo faginctur," is hard to read; the hyphen in "e-rant" may be a printed mark. The word "ut ipse uocat" is set without a printed hyphen across the line end, so it is written whole. The short s is printed as a plain s throughout; i/j and u/v are normalised as the rules say. The reading "subiiciam" is taken from the j-like letter, which is a vowel.
